messages.author: 1ec981f6ad974842
messages.subject: Specify library?
parts:
Hi all,

I have a general question about proper R installation housekeeping - is there an advantage to specifying the library directory where your R packages are installed?  Every time I install a new package, it gets stored in a temporary folder - this has never been a problem (even when installing new versions of R) because it's always possible to copy them over, but I was just wondering if I'm committing a housekeeping faux pas by never specifying a library.  Are there best practices for this?  

Also, only slightly related, but for anyone who uses R on Windows machines, have you ever run into trouble with Rtools being installed in the Program Files directory?

Thanks!

Myfanwy

messages.author: ecf19e9eac4d03c4
messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: Specify library?
parts:
Hi Myfanwy,

That's a good question.

I don't know about best practices, but there are scenarios where you might need to specify directories in which to install packages. For instance, there was a time when there were 2 versions of lme4 that I was using (back when they were about to release their overhaul of the package to CRAN), and I purposefully installed each in different directories specifically loaded the one I needed.

HTH,
Dan.

messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: Specify library?
parts:
I personally install all my libraries into my Dropbox folder (I just have to remember to pause Sync while I install). I also run R and RStudio from my DB. That way I don't have to worry about different versions of packages being installed across the three computers I most frequently use. 


And I think only the actual downloaded zip files are stored in the temporary location, the packages themselves are installed into your actual library. Where that's at I can't say. I don't even know where the default location is.
